text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
-- Upward pressure on fuel prices. A new price hike at the end of the month due to increased production costs resulting from the reduction in sulfur content
-- The government will toughen its stance on the issue of tax breaks by eliminating half of the existing 824 ones
-- Dissapointing scenarios from the inflation front. In search for measures to contain price increases
-- The new budget foresees a 12.5 increase in tax revenues and a significant increase in spending
-- The contract to award the Rhodes casino licence is likely to be signed today. Playboy, Michaniki, state Commercial Bank and two Greek families make up the winning consortium
-- Austere measures for insurance companies. Solvency ratios to change
-- Tax revenues rose by just 2.0 percent in September
-- Secrecy about the new sources of tax revenues. The finance ministry will announce them when it submits the 1997 budget
-- The interbank market expects liquidity to be restored quickly
-- The government studies ways to chnage the social insurance system and is sceptical about incomes policy in the public sector
-- Closer to EU convergence with "accounting" gains
-- The Greek industrialists suggest to government officials to achieve a primary surplus equal to six percent of GDP in 1997
